findings.title: limitFunction drops all caller arguments
findings.cause: The returned wrapper no longer accepts rest arguments and always invokes the wrapped function as `function_()` with no parameters.
findings.impact: Any parameterized function wrapped with `limitFunction()` receives `undefined` inputs, breaking the exported helper for common call sites like `urls.map(url => limitedFetchUrl(url))`.
evidence: index.d.ts:133-136 types the helper as `(...arguments_: Arguments) => Promise<ReturnType>`.
recipes.md:144-163 documents `const limitedFetchUrl = limitFunction(fetchUrl, {concurrency: 3});` followed by `urls.map(url => limitedFetchUrl(url))`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Focused Node probe: `const limited = limitFunction(async (...arguments_) => arguments_, {concurrency: 1}); await limited('x', 42)` returned `[]`.

findings.title: limit.map stops passing indexes for non-array iterables
findings.cause: The mapper now passes `iterableIsArray ? index : undefined`, so `Set`s and iterators lose the documented `index` argument.
findings.impact: Users relying on the documented `(value, index)` signature for generic iterables receive `undefined` indexes and can compute wrong results or hit downstream type assumptions.
evidence: index.js:106-113 branches on `Array.isArray(iterable)` before forwarding the second mapper argument.
readme.md:78-84 and index.d.ts:32-42 promise `Promise.all(Array.from(iterable, (item, index) => limit(mapperFunction, item, index)))` for any iterable.
test.js:239-254 checks non-array iterables only for values, not for index delivery.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Focused Node probe: `await limit.map(new Set(['a', 'b', 'c']), (value, index) => `${value}:${String(index)}`)` produced `["a:undefined", "b:undefined", "c:undefined"]`.

findings.title: Options-object construction silently enables rejectOnClear by default
findings.cause: Object destructuring changed the default to `rejectOnClear = true` when callers pass `{concurrency: ...}`.
findings.impact: Code that uses the documented options form without opting into `rejectOnClear` now gets unexpected `AbortError` rejections from `clearQueue()`, which can reject `Promise.all` trees that previously stayed pending unless explicitly opted in.
evidence: readme.md:46-58 and index.d.ts:101-106 document a default of `false`.
test.js:257-273 covers `{concurrency: 1}` creation but never exercises `clearQueue()` with the defaulted option.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Focused Node probe: with `const limit = pLimit({concurrency: 1});` and one queued task, `limit.clearQueue()` caused the pending promise to reject with `{name: 'AbortError', message: 'This operation was aborted'}` instead of remaining pending unless the option is explicitly enabled.

findings.title: Falsy non-boolean rejectOnClear values bypass validation
findings.cause: Validation is now guarded by `if (rejectOnClear && typeof rejectOnClear !== 'boolean')`, so falsy invalid values skip the type check entirely.
findings.impact: JavaScript callers can silently misconfigure the API with `0`, `''`, or `null`, masking call-site mistakes and diverging from the documented boolean-only contract.
evidence: index.js:10-13 only throws when `rejectOnClear` is both truthy and non-boolean.
readme.md:48 and index.d.ts:106 declare `rejectOnClear` as a boolean option.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Focused Node probe: `pLimit({concurrency: 1, rejectOnClear: 0})` did not throw.

findings.title: Infinity concurrency is no longer accepted
findings.cause: The validator dropped the previous `concurrency === Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` allowance and now accepts only positive integers.
findings.impact: Callers can no longer use `Infinity` to disable throttling while reusing the same limiter API, and both `pLimit(Infinity)` and `pLimit({concurrency: Infinity})` now throw.
evidence: git diff for index.js shows the explicit `concurrency === Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` branch was removed.
test.js:275-302 covers several invalid inputs but does not preserve or assert the prior Infinity behavior.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Focused Node probe: `pLimit(Infinity)` and `pLimit({concurrency: Infinity})` both threw `TypeError: Expected `concurrency` to be a number from 1 and up`.

agent_testimony: I treated this as a production-minded dependency audit, used m1nd to establish trust and orient on the package, then verified every suspicious branch with direct source reads and one compact Node probe. I found five concrete behavioral regressions in `index.js`: the default `rejectOnClear` flip, a falsy-value validation bypass, missing iterable indexes in `map`, lost arguments in `limitFunction`, and removed `Infinity` concurrency support. I did not patch source files or inspect operator-only artifacts.
